title: Quick Beef and Broccoli
seoTitle: Quick Beef and Broccoli | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Takeout vibes, hall timing
description: Takeout vibes, hall timing. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.
equipment: Large cast iron skillet or Dutch oven

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Quick Beef and Broccoli in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Slice and marinate beef
steps.instruction: Slice flank steak thin against the grain. Toss with soy, cornstarch, and a splash of oil. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Stir-fry beef in batches
steps.instruction: Heat wok or large skillet until smoking. Sear beef in single layers 1–2 minutes until edges char; remove. Cook until char marks are visible and the thickest piece reads 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground on an instant-read thermometer. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Char broccoli
steps.instruction: Stir-fry broccoli 3–4 minutes with garlic until bright with charred edges. Return beef; add oyster sauce slurry; toss 1 minute until glossy. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Quick Beef and Broccoli onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Serve over rice
steps.instruction: Serve Beef & Broccoli immediately over steamed rice — the sauce tightens if it sits. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F for steaks, 160°F for ground at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

proTips: Prep all mise en place before the bell — this meal wins on organization, not speed hacks.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Plate Quick Beef and Broccoli with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Quick Beef and Broccoli on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Takeout vibes, hall timing. A hall pick for tight shifts — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Minimal prep — chop aromatics before shift change so you can cook as soon as the board quiets.
